wax-chandler.d: one who deals in wax candles

waxing.d: pertaining to the period during which the visible surface of the moon increases

wax light.d: stick of wax with a wick in the middle

wax paper.d: paper that has been waterproofed by treatment with wax or paraffin

wax figure.d: an effigy (usually of a famous person) made of wax

wax plant.d: succulent climber of southern Asia with umbels of pink and white star-shaped flowers

wax moth.d: moth whose larvae live in and feed on bee honeycombs

wax palm.d: South American palm yielding a wax similar to carnauba wax

wax insect.d: any of various insects that secrete a waxy substance

wax myrtle.d: any shrub or small tree of the genus Myrica with aromatic foliage and small wax-coated berries

wax mallow.d: any of various plants of the genus Malvaviscus having brilliant bell-shaped drooping flowers like incompletely opened hibiscus flowers

wax begonia.d: hybrid fibrous-rooted begonia having broad-ovate green to bronze-red leaves and small clusters of white or pink or red flowers; widely used as a bedding plant

wax crayon.d: writing implement consisting of a colored stick of composition wax used for writing and drawing

waxiness.d: the quality of being made of wax or covered with wax

waxy.d: capable of being bent or flexed or twisted without breaking

waxwing.d: brown velvety-plumaged songbirds of the northern hemisphere having crested heads and red waxy wing tips

waxwork.d: twining shrub of North America having yellow capsules enclosing scarlet seeds

waxflower.d: small waxy white or pinkish-white saprophytic woodland plant having scalelike leaves and a nodding flower; turns black with age

waxycap.d: any fungus of the family Hygrophoraceae having gills that are more or less waxy in appearance

waxmallow.d: any of various plants of the genus Malvaviscus having brilliant bell-shaped drooping flowers like incompletely opened hibiscus flowers

waxberry.d: deciduous aromatic shrub of eastern North America with grey-green wax-coated berries
